database_summary: This is a small transactional music store schema (Chinook-like) in SQLite. It models artists, albums, tracks and related catalog metadata (genres, media types, playlists) plus customers, employees, invoices and invoice line items. Row counts indicate a relatively small catalog (artists/albums/tracks) and transactional history (invoices, invoice_items, playlist_track). Referential integrity is expressed via foreign keys. Many tables are descriptive (dimensions/entities); invoice/invoice_items are transactional facts. Joins between catalog and transactional tables can multiply rows (one invoice -> many invoice_items; one track -> many playlist entries).

accepted.name: invoice_items_enriched
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  ii.InvoiceLineId,
  ii.InvoiceId,
  ii.TrackId,
  ii.UnitPrice,
  ii.Quantity,
  (ii.UnitPrice * ii.Quantity) AS LineTotal,
  inv.CustomerId,
  inv.InvoiceDate,
  inv.BillingCountry,
  inv.Total AS InvoiceTotal,
  cust.FirstName,
  cust.LastName,
  cust.Country AS CustomerCountry,
  cust.SupportRepId,
  tr.Name AS Name,
  tr.AlbumId,
  tr.MediaTypeId,
  tr.GenreId,
  tr.Composer,
  tr.Milliseconds,
  tr.Bytes,
  tr.UnitPrice AS TrackUnitPrice,
  alb.Title AS Title,
  alb.ArtistId,
  art.Name AS ArtistName,
  g.Name AS GenreName,
  mt.Name AS MediaTypeName
FROM invoice_items ii
LEFT JOIN invoices inv ON ii.InvoiceId = inv.InvoiceId
LEFT JOIN customers cust ON inv.CustomerId = cust.CustomerId
LEFT JOIN tracks tr ON ii.TrackId = tr.TrackId
LEFT JOIN albums alb ON tr.AlbumId = alb.AlbumId
LEFT JOIN artists art ON alb.ArtistId = art.ArtistId
LEFT JOIN genres g ON tr.GenreId = g.GenreId
LEFT JOIN media_types mt ON tr.MediaTypeId = mt.MediaTypeId
accepted.description: Denormalized invoice line items with linked invoice, customer, track, album, artist, genre and media type attributes. Use this when you need line-level sales with contextual metadata (customer, track, album, artist, genre, media type) for aggregation, filtering, or reporting. | Use for: Top-selling tracks by revenue or quantity; Customer purchase history at line-item level; Sales by genre / artist / album / media type; Join-level validation between invoice totals and line totals

accepted.name: customer_invoices_agg
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  inv.CustomerId,
  COUNT(inv.InvoiceId) AS InvoiceCount,
  SUM(inv.Total) AS TotalRevenue,
  AVG(inv.Total) AS AvgInvoiceTotal,
  MIN(inv.InvoiceDate) AS FirstInvoiceDate,
  MAX(inv.InvoiceDate) AS LastInvoiceDate
FROM invoices inv
GROUP BY inv.CustomerId
accepted.description: Invoice-level aggregated metrics per customer: invoice count, sum of invoice totals, average invoice total, first and last invoice dates. Use for customer lifetime value, recency/frequency/monetary calculations, or cohorting. | Use for: Customer lifetime value and RFM analysis; Segment customers by revenue or activity; Reports showing top customers by revenue or invoice count

accepted.name: track_catalog
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  tr.TrackId,
  tr.Name,
  tr.AlbumId,
  tr.MediaTypeId,
  tr.GenreId,
  tr.Composer,
  tr.Milliseconds,
  tr.Bytes,
  tr.UnitPrice,
  alb.Title AS Title,
  alb.ArtistId,
  art.Name AS ArtistName,
  g.Name AS GenreName,
  mt.Name AS MediaTypeName
FROM tracks tr
LEFT JOIN albums alb ON tr.AlbumId = alb.AlbumId
LEFT JOIN artists art ON alb.ArtistId = art.ArtistId
LEFT JOIN genres g ON tr.GenreId = g.GenreId
LEFT JOIN media_types mt ON tr.MediaTypeId = mt.MediaTypeId
accepted.description: Catalog of tracks enriched with album, artist, genre and media type attributes. Useful for catalog listings, content analytics, and joining to transactional tables. | Use for: Catalog inventory and metadata reports; Filter tracks by artist/genre/media type; Join tracks to sales for top-selling content

accepted.name: playlist_membership_counts
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  pt.TrackId,
  COUNT(pt.PlaylistId) AS PlaylistCount
FROM playlist_track pt
GROUP BY pt.TrackId
accepted.description: Counts of how many playlists each track is a member of and how many tracks each playlist contains. Useful for popularity signals and playlist analytics. | Use for: Identify popular tracks by playlist inclusion; Correlate playlist presence with sales

accepted.name: employee_hierarchy
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  e.EmployeeId,
  e.LastName,
  e.FirstName,
  e.Title,
  e.ReportsTo,
  0 AS Depth,
  CAST(e.EmployeeId AS TEXT) AS Path
FROM employees e
WHERE e.ReportsTo IS NULL
UNION ALL
SELECT
  e2.EmployeeId,
  e2.LastName,
  e2.FirstName,
  e2.Title,
  e2.ReportsTo,
  eh.Depth + 1 AS Depth,
  eh.Path || '>' || CAST(e2.EmployeeId AS TEXT) AS Path
FROM employees e2
JOIN employee_hierarchy eh ON e2.ReportsTo = eh.EmployeeId
accepted.description: Recursive hierarchy of employees showing reporting chains (manager -> subordinate) through the ReportsTo relationship. Useful for org-chart queries, management chain lookups, and roll-ups by manager. | Use for: Find all subordinates under a manager; Compute depth in organization or reporting chains

accepted.name: employees_with_reports_count
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  mgr.EmployeeId,
  mgr.LastName,
  mgr.FirstName,
  COUNT(e.EmployeeId) AS DirectReportCount
FROM employees mgr
LEFT JOIN employees e ON e.ReportsTo = mgr.EmployeeId
GROUP BY mgr.EmployeeId, mgr.LastName, mgr.FirstName
accepted.description: Direct report counts for each employee (number of employees that report to them). Useful for org metrics and workload distribution. | Use for: Identify managers with many direct reports; Org structure summaries

accepted.name: invoice_line_amounts_by_invoice
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  ii.InvoiceId,
  SUM(ii.UnitPrice * ii.Quantity) AS LinesTotal,
  SUM(ii.Quantity) AS TotalQuantity,
  COUNT(ii.InvoiceLineId) AS LineCount
FROM invoice_items ii
GROUP BY ii.InvoiceId
accepted.description: Aggregate invoice line totals per invoice: sum of line amounts and total quantity. Use to validate invoice header totals or analyze invoice composition. | Use for: Reconcile invoice header Total vs. sum of lines; Analyze invoice complexity and item counts

accepted.name: active_customers
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.CustomerId,
  c.FirstName,
  c.LastName,
  c.Email,
  c.Country,
  c.SupportRepId
FROM customers c
WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM invoices inv WHERE inv.CustomerId = c.CustomerId)
accepted.description: Subset of customers that have at least one invoice. Use when analyzing paying or transacting customers (cohort selection). This is a cohort derived by existence of invoices rather than a literal flag. | Use for: Analyze customers who made purchases; Target customers for re-engagement who have never purchased (complement)

accepted.name: tracks_sales_agg
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  ii.TrackId,
  SUM(ii.Quantity) AS TotalQuantitySold,
  SUM(ii.UnitPrice * ii.Quantity) AS TotalRevenue,
  COUNT(DISTINCT ii.InvoiceId) AS DistinctInvoiceCount
FROM invoice_items ii
GROUP BY ii.TrackId
accepted.description: Aggregated sales metrics per track: total quantity sold, total revenue, and number of distinct invoices. Useful for ranking tracks by revenue or units sold. | Use for: Top-selling tracks by revenue/units; Correlation of track popularity with playlist presence

accepted.name: customer_support_rep_assignments
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.CustomerId,
  c.FirstName,
  c.LastName,
  c.Email,
  c.Country AS CustomerCountry,
  c.SupportRepId,
  e.LastName AS RepLastName,
  e.FirstName AS RepFirstName,
  e.Title AS RepTitle,
  e.Email AS RepEmail
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN employees e ON c.SupportRepId = e.EmployeeId
accepted.description: Customers with their assigned support representative (employee) details. Useful for routing, support workload analysis, and regional rep assignments. | Use for: Support rep workload and customer assignments; List customers by rep for outreach

accepted.name: albums_with_track_counts
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  alb.AlbumId,
  alb.Title,
  alb.ArtistId,
  COUNT(tr.TrackId) AS TrackCount,
  SUM(tr.Milliseconds) AS TotalMilliseconds,
  SUM(tr.Bytes) AS TotalBytes
FROM albums alb
LEFT JOIN tracks tr ON tr.AlbumId = alb.AlbumId
GROUP BY alb.AlbumId, alb.Title, alb.ArtistId
accepted.description: Album-level track counts and total duration/size. Useful for album completeness checks and content summaries. | Use for: Album completeness and size reports; Aggregate track durations per album/artist
